items.stem: While performing an endoscopy on a patient with long-term gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) you notice an area of erythema around the distal third of the oesophagus. Which of the following pathological processes has most likely occurred?
items.explanation: Patients with gastro-oesophageal reflux disease (GORD) reflux gastric acid into the distal oesophagus. The acid causes inflammation to the oesophagus, and if the exposure is severe and chronic enough, metaplastic transformation may take place. Metaplasia is the term used to describe the process where one differentiated cell type is replaced with another. The process is reversible and so, if the irritant is removed, the tissue may return to normal.
items.prompt:
Create a landscape 3:2 image (1536x1024). Picmonic-style visual mnemonic, fun and medically accurate, for medical students: cute cartoon characters with big friendly eyes, bright flat colors, thick dark outlines, clean pale background, each fact drawn as a memorable visual pun. All text sits in rounded white label boxes with dark navy bold letters, crisp and spelled exactly as given.
Title banner at the top: "GORD to Metaplasia".
LEFT: a cartoon stomach character squirting a fountain of acid up a tube (the lower oesophagus), the tube wall red and angry. Label: "Acid reflux (GORD)". Label on the red tube end: "Distal oesophagus".
CENTER: the tube wall tiles are being swapped: round pink tiles are replaced by tough grey armour tiles by a little builder, a curved arrow showing one cell type replaced by another. Label: "One cell type replaced".
RIGHT: a big shape-shifting chameleon wearing a hard hat (metaplasia) stands on the swapped tiles; a turn-back arrow shows it can go back if the acid tap is closed. Labels: "Metaplasia", "Reversible".
Crossed-out small signs for the wrong options: "Neoplasia", "Dysplasia".
Bottom banner: "Answer --> Metaplasia".
Avoid: garbled or misspelled text, duplicated characters, distorted faces, realistic gore, photographs, watermarks, cluttered dark background.

items.stem: The following tumour markers are correctly paired with an associated neoplasia except:
items.explanation:
Parathyroid carcinoma may lead to an increase in parathyroid hormone (PTH) production. Further examples of tumour markers include:

Pituitary: Adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH), growth hormone, prolactin Adrenal: Cortisol Carcinoid: 5-Hydroxyindoleacetic acid (5-HIAA) Oat cell: ACTH, antidiuretic hormone Prostate: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) Hepatic: α-Fetoprotein (AFP) (Note: Also cirrhosis, pregnancy, hepatitis, neural tube defect) Colorectal: Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), Ca 19-9 (advanced) Testicular teratoma: β-hCG, CEA, AFP Testicular seminoma: Placental alkaline phosphatase Breast: Ca 15-3 Pancreatic: Ca 19-9 Thyroid: Thyroglobulin, calcitonin (medullary carcinoma) Phaeochromocytoma: Vanillylmandelic acid
